newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER WINS TO BOOST TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER WINS TO BOOST TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Michael Schumacher extended his world championship lead to 14 points with a crushing victory in the French Grand Prix on Sunday.
The 28-year-old German, driving a Ferrari, finished 23.5 seconds ahead of compatriot Heinz-Harald Frentzen in a Williams. Ferrari team mate Eddie Irvine of Britain was third.

The victory was Schumacher's second in succession, third in four races this season and the 25th of his career, a total which put him level with Briton Jim Clark and Austrian Niki Lauda in the record books.
Only four men have won more races than Schumacher and he is now favourite to land his third world title.
He has 47 points in the drivers' championship ahead of nearest rival Canadian Jacques Villeneuve, who was fourth in his Williams, on 33.

Irvine moved up to third in the title race by finishing third after a dramatic closing lap on which Briton David Coulthard spun off in his McLaren and Villeneuve survived an off-track excursion as rain made the final laps tricky.
Frenchman Jean Alesi finished fifth in a Benetton ahead of Schumacher's younger brother, 21-year-old Ralf, who was sixth for Jordan.
The result confirmed Ferrari as clear leaders of the constructors' championship at the halfway stage of the season.
